The purpose of this study was to determine the effect of gravity on the signal intensity (SI), T1, T2, and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) in the lung parenchyma of healthy volunteers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
gravity‐dependent changes of SI are a major source of signal inhomogeneity on MR images of lung parenchyma in supine and in prone body positions.
the lung signal is more sensitive to changes in body position when the lung is in the supine position than when it is in the prone position.
the signal gradient in the supine lung is larger than in the prone lung, and that the magnitude of this signal gradient is proportional to the magnitude of the isogravitational gradient.
